name: Pesarattu

ingredients.name: Whole green moong (sabut moong / green gram, pesalu)
Raw rice (any short-grain or sona masoori)
Ginger (adrak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 cm piece, peeled and roughly chopped

ingredients.name: Cumin seeds (jeera)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ tsp (¼ tsp in the batter + ¼ tsp on top)

ingredients.name: Water, for grinding
ingredients.householdMeasure: about ⅓ cup + 1 tbsp, added little by little

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium onion, finely chopped (about 3 tbsp)

ingredients.name: Oil (groundnut or sunflower)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 tsp in total: ¼ tsp to grease + ¾ tsp to drizzle, per pesarattu

equipment: Flat tawa, cast iron or non-stick, at least 24 cm
Flat spatula (turner) and a ladle (or a ½-cup measure)
A bowl for soaking, a sieve or colander for draining
Knife, chopping board, small bowl for the topping
Half an onion or a folded paper towel for greasing the tawa
Measuring cups and spoons (a normal teacup and teaspoons are fine stand-ins)

steps.title: Measure the moong and rice
steps.text: Put 60 g (⅓ cup) whole green moong and 10 g (1 tbsp) raw rice in a bowl.
steps.visualCue: Green beans with a few white rice grains.
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl of moong and rice
steps.videoShot: Moong poured from a cup into a steel bowl.

steps.title: Wash
steps.text: Cover with water, rub between your palms, pour off the water. Repeat 2 more times.
steps.visualCue: The last rinse water is almost clear; any floating husks or bad beans are poured off.
steps.cameraCheck: The washed moong in clear water
steps.videoShot: Hands rubbing the beans in water.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Cover with about 3 cm of fresh water and leave to soak.
steps.tip: Under-soaked moong grinds gritty and the pesarattu tears.
steps.visualCue: The beans have swollen to about double, some skins are wrinkled, and a bean crushes easily between your fingers.
steps.videoShot: A soaked bean pressed flat between thumb and finger.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain the moong and rice in a sieve and discard the soaking water.
steps.visualCue: Plump, wet beans in the sieve.
steps.videoShot: Water streaming out of the sieve.

steps.title: Load the jar
steps.text: Put the moong and rice in the small mixer jar with 5 g chopped ginger, 4 g green chilli, ¼ tsp cumin and 1.4 g (a scant ¼ tsp) salt.
steps.visualCue: Beans with ginger and chilli pieces on top.
steps.videoShot: Ginger and chilli dropped into the jar.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Add 60 ml water and grind in short bursts, scraping down once, then add the remaining 30 ml little by little until smooth.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, pale green batter with only very fine flecks of skin; rubbed between your fingers it feels only slightly grainy.
steps.videoShot: The batter swirling in the jar.

steps.title: Check the consistency
steps.text: Pour the batter into a bowl and lift a ladle. It should flow like dosa batter: thick but spreadable, coating the back of the spoon. If it is too thick to spread, stir in 1 tbsp water.
steps.tip: Runny batter will not crisp and will tear when you lift it; too thick and it will not spread.
steps.visualCue: A thick ribbon that settles back in 2–3 seconds; about 230 g (a little over 1 cup) of batter.
steps.videoShot: The ribbon of green batter falling back into the bowl.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop 30 g onion (¼ medium onion).
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped onion on the board

steps.title: Chop the coriander
steps.text: Finely chop 3 g (2 tsp) coriander leaves and mix them with the onion and the remaining ¼ tsp cumin. Split the mix into 2 equal heaps.
steps.visualCue: Two small heaps of onion flecked with green and cumin.
steps.videoShot: The topping tossed with a spoon.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat the tawa on medium-high for about 2 min.
steps.visualCue: A few drops of water sprinkled on it sizzle and vanish in 2–3 seconds.
steps.videoShot: Water drops dancing on the tawa.

steps.title: Grease and cool slightly
steps.text: Rub ¼ tsp oil over the tawa with half an onion or a paper towel, then lower the heat to medium.
steps.visualCue: A thin, even sheen of oil, just starting to smoke at the edges is too hot; wait a few seconds.
steps.videoShot: Half an onion rubbed across the tawa.

steps.title: Pour and spread
steps.text: Pour half the batter (about 115 g, ½ cup) in the centre and quickly spread it outwards in a spiral with the back of the ladle into a 22–23 cm circle.
steps.tip: Spread it in one go; going back over setting batter tears it.
steps.visualCue: A thin, even green circle; a few small holes are fine.
steps.cameraCheck: The batter circle on the tawa

steps.title: Add the topping
steps.text: Scatter one heap of onion topping over the wet batter and press it in lightly with the spatula.
steps.visualCue: The onion is half sunk into the batter.
steps.videoShot: The spatula pressing onion into the batter.

steps.title: Drizzle the oil
steps.text: Drizzle ¾ tsp oil around the edge and a few drops over the top.
steps.visualCue: The oil sizzles around the edge.
steps.videoShot: A spoon tracing oil around the rim.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Cook on medium without touching it.
steps.tip: Pesarattu needs a little longer than a plain dosa; lifting too early tears it.
steps.visualCue: The edges turn golden and lift from the tawa, the top looks dry and no longer shiny, and the base is golden brown in spots.
steps.cameraCheck: The edge lifted with the spatula
steps.videoShot: The spatula sliding under a crisp golden edge.

steps.title: Flip (optional) and cook the top
steps.text: Flip and cook the onion side for 30–45 seconds, pressing lightly.
steps.visualCue: The onion turns light brown and smells sweet; no raw onion smell.
steps.cameraCheck: The onion side on the tawa

steps.title: Fold and plate
steps.text: Flip it back (onion side up), fold it in half and slide it onto a plate.
steps.cameraCheck: The folded pesarattu on the plate
steps.videoShot: The pesarattu folded and lifted off.

steps.title: Make the second pesarattu
steps.text: Sprinkle a little water on the tawa to cool it, wipe it, and repeat steps 11–17 with the rest of the batter, topping and oil.
steps.tip: If the batter clumps instead of spreading, the tawa is too hot; the water sprinkle fixes it.
steps.visualCue: A second pesarattu matching the first (often thinner and crisper than the first).
steps.videoShot: The two pesarattu side by side.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately with ginger chutney or coconut chutney (and upma, if you want the full Andhra breakfast).
steps.videoShot: A piece torn off and dipped in chutney.

reasons: a whole-pulse crepe cooked on a tawa with 2 tsp oil, not fried; about 15 g protein and 11.5 g fibre for 340 kcal, rich in folate, iron, magnesium and potassium, no cholesterol or added sugar, moderate salt (about 1.4 g), and the whole moong gives a low-to-moderate glycaemic response. No fermentation is needed. Against it: moong protein is low in methionine (pairing with rice or a dairy side helps), and it is low in vitamins A, C and B12. Restaurant versions are often cooked with ghee or butter, saltier, served with upma (refined rava) and coconut chutney, which push it to 500–700 kcal.

researchRating.basis: a beloved Andhra breakfast with a long tradition (Wikipedia; "MLA pesarattu" is famous in Hyderabad), widely praised as a high-protein, no-fermentation dosa by health writers (Dr. Mohan's) and covered by every major Indian recipe site (Swasthi's Indian Healthy Recipes, Veg Recipes of India with 13+ comment pages, Tarla Dalal, Hebbar's Kitchen, Saffron Trail, Cooking From Heart, Sharmi's Passions). It is less known and less available in Mumbai than masala dosa, and beginners often report tearing or sticking batter. Recipe vote counts could not be checked (pages blocked).

storage: Cooked pesarattu is best fresh; it turns soft and leathery as it cools. Fridge: up to 1 day in an airtight box, within 2 hours of cooking. Freezer: not recommended. Reheat on a hot tawa for 30–60 seconds per side with a few drops of oil; avoid the microwave, which makes it rubbery. Uncooked batter: fridge 1–2 days in a closed box (est.); it slowly sours and thickens, so thin it with a spoon of water. Not suited to freezing (texture turns watery; est.).
leftoverRemix: Pesarattu Frankie Roll. Warm a leftover pesarattu on the tawa, spread 1 tsp green chutney, fill with 50 g crumbled paneer (or tofu) sautéed with onion, capsicum and a pinch of chaat masala, roll tightly and wrap the bottom in foil: a high-protein lunchbox wrap. Leftover batter makes moong paniyaram: stir in chopped onion and coriander and cook in a greased appe pan for 3–4 min per side.
burnOff: about 4.9 km of running (340 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 6.8 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 20 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With chutney and upma (about +200–250 kcal), add about 3–3.5 km of running.

navratri.reason: the batter is whole moong (a pulse) and rice, both avoided on the common North and West Indian vrat rule set, and it is topped with onion

ekadashi.reason: rice and pulses (moong) are the foods given up on the common Ekadashi rule set

jain.reason: skip the fresh ginger and onion; moong, rice, green chilli, cumin and coriander fit common Jain practice (check family practice on dry ginger)

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so there is no halal concern; high in protein and fibre (about 15 g and 11 g), which keeps you full at sehri, with moderate salt (about 1.4 g)

jain.reason: skip the fresh ginger (a root) and the onion topping; use a pinch of dry ginger powder (sonth) or just chilli and cumin, and coriander leaves

vegan.reason: moong, rice, spices, onion and oil only; restaurant "ghee pesarattu" versions are not vegan

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, fish or egg, so it fits a pescatarian diet

sattvik.reason: skip the onion topping (no garlic is used); ginger, chilli and cumin stay

glutenFree.reason: whole green moong and rice, no wheat, rava or hing in the main recipe; many recipes add hing, and most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour, so add it only if it is labelled gluten-free; the upma-filled version is not gluten-free (rava)

dairyFree.reason: cooked in oil, no ghee, butter or curd

description: A vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and dairy-free Andhra crepe of ground whole green moong, ginger and chilli; Jain, sattvik and upma-filled versions below.
